summary: Backend regression tests for non-destructive photo re-cropping (original_data). Wrote 16 pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_photo_original_data.py covering upload with/without original_data, list omission, GET /original, PATCH preservation, PATCH back-fill on legacy rows, public user leak check, anonymous 403 rejections, and delete/set-primary regression. All 16/16 pass against http://localhost:8001. One minor spec deviation flagged (has_original semantics).

minor.issue: Spec says `has_original` should be true only when the record has a DISTINCT uncropped source, but implementation returns `bool(doc.get('original_data'))`. Because upload without original_data now populates original_data = data (fallback), every new photo returns `has_original: true` even when there is no true zoom-out available. Suggest either (a) not populating original_data on fallback and treating missing field as `has_original=false`, or (b) computing `has_original = doc.get('original_data') is not None and doc.get('original_data') != doc.get('data')`. Current behavior is consistent for the cropper (it always gets a usable payload) so this is low priority — clients just cannot distinguish 'true zoom-out available' from 'reposition-only'.

action_items: Review the has_original semantics vs the spec (see minor issue). If the intent is for clients to skip fetching /original when there is nothing new to zoom-out to, adjust the return value or stop populating original_data on fallback.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py `_reject_if_anonymous` is correctly invoked on POST /auth/me/photos, PATCH /auth/me/photos/{id}, PATCH /primary, DELETE, and GET /original.
PATCH replace_photo correctly guards back-fill with `if body.original_data and not photo.get('original_data')` — writes original_data only when absent.
PhotoUploadBody enforces min_length=40 on both data and original_data — good sanity guard.
3.5MB base64 cap enforced separately on data and original_data — good.
